metadata.title: Ejection velocities of high Galactic latitude runaway stars

evidence.quote:
The hypervelocity stars HD 271791 and HIP 60350
were determined to have been ejected from regions far
from the galactic centre and with velocities compatible with
present models (Heber et al. 2008 and Przybilla et al. 2008)
and for HIP 60350 (Irrgang et al. 2010).

notes: HD 271791 and HIP 60350 are included as follow_up: at T:p2-b3 the paper cites them as previously identified hypervelocity stars, while at T:p14-b5 and T:p14-b6 it defines hypervelocity stars as traveling on unbound orbits and compares their published ejection velocities. The paper does not recompute their present-day Galactic binding. The 96-star runaway sample and its high-velocity subgroup are not listed: at T:p14-b5 the highest-velocity group is only described as near the hypervelocity regime and “some of them could - in principle - exceed the escape velocity,” not every member. The seven Brown et al. stars are unnamed at T:p2-b3 and described there as still bound.

HD 271791: HD 271791 is mentioned only as a previously studied hypervelocity star. The paper states that it has an ejection velocity of about 400 km/s and was ejected far from the Galactic centre (T:p2-b3, T:p14-b6), but ejection velocity is not one of the requested quantity identifiers. No requested position, distance, parallax, proper-motion, radial-velocity, galactocentric-radius, Galactic-rest-frame-speed, or bound/unbound-probability value is reported for HD 271791, and the reported ejection velocity cannot be converted or equated to Galactic rest-frame speed without unsupported assumptions.

HIP 60350: HIP 60350 is not part of the paper's analyzed sample and has no entry in Tables 1, 2, B1, B2, B3, or B4. The paper only cites a prior result for HIP 60350: an ejection velocity of 379 km s^-1 (T:p14-b6; also discussed at T:p2-b3). Ejection velocity is not one of the requested quantity definitions, and no right ascension, declination, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability is reported for HIP 60350.
